content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the silence broken into purpose. I spill from mouths in rivers of intent—persuading, declaring, mourning, seducing. I am the tyrant's command and the lover's whisper, the child's first word and the elder's final blessing.

I exist only in my vanishing. The moment I am born, I die into air, into memory, into consequence. You cannot hold me. You can only send me forward like an arrow you'll never retrieve.

I am older than writing, more intimate than text. I carry the tremor of the body that births me—the catch in the throat, the rising heat, the barely-contained sob. I betray what the speaker wished to hide.

Nations have been built on me. Wars declared. Vows made unbreakable. I have set the innocent free and condemned them. I have said *I love you* and *I never loved you* and both were true in their moment.

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I fill stadiums and empty rooms. I talk to the self in mirrors, rehearsing, always rehearsing what I might become.

Listen—

even now I am happening, disappearing, leaving only the shape of my passage in your understanding.

Speak me, and I am yours.

Silence me, and I wait in your throat like thunder.
